# The Housing Helpline

> Claims management company helping tenants in England with housing disrepair and tenancy deposit claims. The Housing Helpline is part of Claim 3000 Ltd (Manchester, FCA firm reference 833604, regulated for housing disrepair claims). It checks whether tenants could claim and introduces them to independent regulated solicitors. You do not need to use a claims management company: you can complain to your landlord and then the Housing Ombudsman, or use your deposit scheme's dispute service, for free.

Phone 0161 541 2053 (Monday to Friday, 9am to 5pm). Email contact@claim3000.co.uk.

## Pages

- [Housing disrepair and tenancy deposit claims](/housing-helpline-preview/): Housing disrepair and tenancy deposit claims in England. Check for free whether you could claim compensation, get repairs done, or up to 3 times your deposit.
- [Start my claim](/housing-helpline-preview/check/): Start your housing disrepair or tenancy deposit claim in England. A few quick questions, free and with no obligation.
- [Housing disrepair: your rights](/housing-helpline-preview/your-rights/): What counts as housing disrepair, what your landlord must fix, Awaab's Law deadlines and when you could claim compensation in England.
- [Tenancy deposit claims](/housing-helpline-preview/tenancy-deposits/): What tenancy deposit protection means, the 30-day rules, and how a court can order up to 3 times the deposit if it was not protected.

## Questions and answers

### Is the claim check free?

Yes. The claim check is free and does not commit you to a claim.

### Can I make a claim myself?

Yes. You do not need a claims company. For repairs, complain to your landlord, then the Housing Ombudsman, for free. Housing association tenants can also ask their council's environmental health team. Your deposit scheme offers free dispute resolution. For unprotected or late-protected deposits, you can apply to the county court without a solicitor. A court fee applies, which you can claim back if you win.

### Who handles my claim?

An independent regulated solicitor handles your claim if you go ahead. First, our team checks your situation and explains your options. We then introduce you to the solicitor.

### How long does the claim check take?

The online claim check takes about 60 seconds. We aim to reply within 2 working days.

### Do I need evidence for the claim check?

No. You can start your claim check without evidence. Photos, messages to your landlord and receipts are helpful. We will explain what other information could help.

### What does a claim cost if I go ahead?

The solicitor explains their fees in writing before you agree to go ahead. You can review the terms before deciding to proceed.

### Can my landlord evict me for making a claim?

Since 1 May 2026, a landlord can no longer evict you using a "no fault" section 21 notice. A landlord needs a legal reason, called a ground for possession.

### Is there a time limit for a disrepair claim?

Yes. A disrepair claim usually has a time limit of up to 6 years from when your landlord should have done the work, or 3 years for an injury to your health.

### What is housing disrepair?

Housing disrepair means your landlord has not kept your rented home in repair or fit to live in. The Landlord and Tenant Act 1985 covers the structure, exterior, water, gas, electricity, heating and sanitation. Since 2019, the law also requires your home to be fit to live in throughout the tenancy.

### Can I claim compensation for housing disrepair?

You could claim if you rent from a council or housing association in England, have reported the problem and the repairs are still needed. A claim can lead to compensation and a court order requiring the repairs.

### How much compensation could I get for housing disrepair?

Housing disrepair compensation has no fixed amount. The amount depends on the severity and duration of the problem and its effects on you, including damaged belongings, extra costs and harm to your health.

### What is Awaab's Law?

Awaab's Law sets repair deadlines for council and housing association landlords in England, in force since 27 October 2025. Landlords must make emergency hazards safe within 24 hours, investigate significant damp and mould within 10 working days, and carry out safety work within 5 working days after the investigation.

### How long do I have to make a housing disrepair claim?

A housing disrepair claim usually has a time limit of up to 6 years from when your landlord should have done the work. For an injury to your health, the time limit is 3 years.

### What does tenancy deposit protection mean?

Tenancy deposit protection means your landlord or letting agent puts your deposit in a government-approved scheme within 30 days of receiving the deposit. England's three schemes are the Deposit Protection Service, MyDeposits and the Tenancy Deposit Scheme.

### Can I claim if my deposit was unprotected or protected late?

You could claim if your deposit was unprotected or protected after the 30 days. A court can order your landlord to return or protect your deposit and pay you up to 3 times the deposit.

### What must my landlord tell me about my deposit?

Within 30 days of receiving your deposit, your landlord must give you written details of the scheme, the amount paid, how the deposit is protected, why deductions might be made and how to get your deposit back.

### How long does a landlord have to return my deposit?

Your landlord must return your deposit within 10 days of you both agreeing how much you get back.

### Do deposit rules still apply after 1 May 2026?

Yes. Deposit protection rules still apply after 1 May 2026, when most assured shorthold tenancies became assured periodic tenancies.
